newsitem.title: USA: Calif. home sales off from Nov, up from year ago.
newsitem.headline: Calif. home sales off from Nov, up from year ago.

text.p: California home sales declined slightly in December from the November rate but rose 6.2 percent from the December 1995 sales pace, according to a report released on Monday.

Statewide, 478,140 existing, single-family detached homes closed escrow during December on a seasonally-adjusted, annualized basis, down 3.8 percent from a revised annualized rate of 497,270 homes sold in November, the California Association of Realtors reported.
The December sales pace increased 6.2 percent from the December 1995 annualized rate, when 450,320 homes were sold.

The statewide median price of an existing, single-family detached home sold during December was $171,940, down 2.0 percent from $175,500 in November. The December median price also edged down 2.0 percent from December 1995, when the median-priced home sold for $175,370, according to the report.

"The drop in available inventory may be constraining market activity in some areas, especially those that have experienced significant home price appreciation throughout last year," said Leslie Appleton-Young, vice president of economics at the California Association of Realtors.

"The upscale market in particular has been subject to tight inventory conditions as trade-up buyers have returned to this market segment. This is evident not just in Silicon Valley but also in higher-end neighborhoods in southern California," Appleton-Young said in a statement.
